text:
Priya: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change rolled last night we're seeing intermittent OOMs on long-context requests (16k+). Not consistent but spikes in GPU mem usage right before crash.
Sam: Ugh. Any flamegraphs or profiler output?
Priya: Yep. Quick excerpt from the perf run:
```
[2026-02-16 02:03:12] model=redwood-v2/13b seq=16384 batch=1
allocated_peak=14.7G free_before=512M
kv_cache_alloc=6.1G logits_scratch=3.8G activations=4.2G
kernel_path=optimized-attn-v2 (fallbacks observed to kernel-compat-legacy)
```
Priya: The pattern looks like: optimized kernel picks a layout that allocs many small scratch buffers, causing fragmentation and repeated fallback allocations for KV slices.
Jules: Do we have a repro script? Maybe the kernel changed alignment/stride expectations and our allocator fast-path fails to coalesce.
Priya: Repro is here: `tests/perf/repro_kv_fragmentation.py` — run with `--seq 16000 --num-requests 50`. I can leave it running on the canary.
Kai: I ran one locally — interestingly, the allocator free stats show many small freelist hits but big contiguous chunk requests still go to cudaMalloc. Looks like we never reuse freed subsegments for logits scratch.
Sam: Could be slab size choice. We tuned slabs down to lower tail latency last quarter; maybe too small for long contexts. Slab eviction causes backend to request fresh allocations.
Priya: Agreed. Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) Increase slab size threshold for scratch/logits to prefer larger contiguous blocks; 2) Add coalescing pass on free for small adjacent slots; 3) Temporarily pin kernel selector to pre-change version for dedicated nodes while we patch.
Jules: For 2) coalescing: we need runtime-safe ordering guarantees — coalesce only at safe sync points (end-of-inference) or we risk racing with async streams. Also consider deferring free of KV pages until no outstanding requests reference them (refcount + epoch).
Kai: I ran an experiment toggling `PREFER_CONTIGUOUS_LOGITS=true` — peak mem dropped ~700MB and OOM rate went to 0/50 in the run. Latency delta minimal (+1–2ms p95). Patch looks promising.
Priya: Nice. Can we roll that as a canary feature flag for hosted hosts?
Sam: Yes, feature flag + backstop: if mem usage crosses 90% we trigger fallback to legacy kernels and disable contiguous pref. Also add a perf regression job on CI that runs the repro script nightly.
infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for platform/selector-v2 on cluster-canary-3 by @ci. Logs at https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 :thumbsup:
Jules: I'll draft a short runtime patch: coalesce-at-sync + refcount delay for KV frees. If we can avoid touching kernel selection logic that's safer.
Priya: Sounds good. I'll leave the canary running and post logs in this thread. If anyone sees OOMs in customer canaries ping me directly.
Sam: Thanks — once we have the coalesce patch we should run a few long-seq soak runs (12h) on a dedicated GPU to be sure.
Kai: I'll add the CI nightly job and a small dashboard showing allocated_peak and num-fallback-kernels per host.
Priya: Appreciate it. Filing follow-up issue: https://issues.internal/RED-2741 (notes + repro).
